title: Lab: live charts (light curve, plot wall, V-curve, conditions, visibility, histogram, mini-charts, in context)
summary: Live chart prototypes in web/lab/charts.html (src/lab/charts/), uPlot 1.6 + Canvas 2D, no new dependency, fed by a synthetic but physically shaped night: SW And (an RRab star, synthetic ephemeris) from Paris on 2026-11-01, ~51.5 s cadence like the owner's runs, two autofocus pauses, three cloud passages, a focus loss at 22:16 UTC repaired by the 23:31 autofocus, a satellite trail, a Moon rising after midnight. One simulated clock drives every chart (x1 to x600); shots are taken with the clock paused at 22:41:07 UTC (02:20 for Review) so they are reproducible. Chromium shots: headless Chrome 156, 1440 x 900 (or 1280 x 800), DPR 1. WebKit shots (webkit-*): a real WKWebView of macOS 26.5 through the research lab's probe, 2x. Every Night Red shot was audited pixel by pixel (non-red = max(G, B) > 8 and > 0.68 R): 0 offending pixels in all 13 Chromium and 3 WebKit Night Red shots. Live update cost with 5 000+ points per facet, three facets, one append per frame: median 4.2 ms / p95 4.5 ms in Chrome (DPR 1; 4.0 / 4.5 ms at DPR 2), median 6 ms / p95 7-8 ms in WKWebView at 2x (51-55 fps over two runs). WebKitGTK and WebView2 are not tested. Everything is synthetic: no number here is a measurement.

shots.caption: Light curve, Observatory, 1440 x 900, at 22:41:07 UTC (269 frames). Three facets on one linked UTC axis, one y axis each: target SW And (circles, magnitude inverted, error bars, the newest point ringed), check star minus its catalogue V (triangles, with the trailing 15-point mean ± 1 sigma as a band: rms of the last 60 = 0.006 mag), comparison ensemble instrumental minus catalogue (squares, band = spread of the 5 comparisons). The two cloud dips (19:52, 21:06) dim every star and show in the ensemble facet only: they cancel in the target facet, which is the point of differential photometry. The 20:12 satellite trail is a hollow circle (suspect, flag by shape). 'AF' marks the 20:31 autofocus pause. Header: latest V 9.503 ± 0.007, mode chip 'Whole run'.
Same light curve in Charcoal: role colours and bands read the same on the higher-contrast graphite.
Same light curve in Night Red: the role colours collapse to one hue, roles stay apart by marker shape (circle, triangle, square) and by the facet titles. Night Red audit: 0 non-red pixels.

Interaction: zoomed on 20:40-22:10 (the zoom is linked across facets), a time selected by click (dashed line and rings on every facet, frame 151) and the pointer over 21:32:25. One crosshair runs through the three facets (uPlot cursor sync) and one readout lists every series at that frame with values first: UTC, JD and approximate BJD to 5 decimals, V 9.423 ± 0.004, check +0.012 ± 0.005, ensemble with 5/5 comparisons used, airmass and altitude. The chip says 'Zoom kept · F fits': new frames never move a manual zoom.

Drag-to-zoom in progress on the check facet: the selection (12 % brass wash, brass edges) is mirrored on all three facets because the cursor is synced; the readout follows the pointer (20:52:16 UTC, frame 145). On release the three facets zoom to the same range.

BJD axis and follow mode, Charcoal, clock running at x600. Ticks are BJD_TDB − 2461346 at round fractions of a day (the x scale stays in unix seconds, so switching UTC / JD / BJD keeps the zoom). Follow (End, or the live tool) pins a fixed-width window to the newest frame; new frames slide it. The axis title says the BJD is a lab approximation (heliocentric light time, within about 4 s): the server computes the exact value.

Legend toggles and export hook, Charcoal: 'median of 9' turned on (a trailing median: drawn points never move when new ones arrive, and it visibly lags the fast rise, which is why it is off by default) and the check band turned off (its key greys out). The PNG export hook composes the three canvases and their headers; the toast reports 'Saved … 1440 × 730 px · 111 kB' (the headless download itself was denied by the capture script). TSV copy is the tool next to it.

The same component in the Observe band under the image (928 x 299 px, the size layout.ts gives it at 1440 x 900 with the rail open): one compact toolbar row, target over check on one time axis, the ensemble facet left to the stage and Review.
Observe band size in Night Red. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.
The same component in a 1 348 x 216 px drawer: still two readable facets with 18 px headers; this is the floor. Below it the band's compact one-row form (latest value) is the better answer.

Performance: the 4 s cadence stress run, 5 000 points per facet preloaded, then one new frame per animation frame up to 5 520 (three facets, markers, error bars, band). Chrome 156, DPR 1: update (setData + draw of all facets) median 4.2 ms, p95 4.5 ms, max 5.7 ms over the last 240 updates, 61 fps sustained. Same run at DPR 2: 4.0 / 4.5 / 4.8 ms. In WKWebView (see webkit-curve-stress-observatory): median 6 ms, p95 7-8 ms, max 8-10 ms, 51-55 fps over two runs. At the real cadence (one frame a minute) this cost occurs once a minute.
Light curve at 1280 x 800: the facets keep their proportions, the toolbar keeps its controls (the update-cost chip is the first thing to go).

Reduced motion: the '+' key zoom glide (180 ms, for orientation) is skipped and the view jumps; the shot is taken 40 ms after the key press and already shows the final view. Data never animates in any mode.

Review plot wall at 02:20 UTC (500 frames, the whole run): one star per cell (target, check, C1-C5 leave-one-out residuals, HFD), one linked time axis, a 'session health' strip on top with three lanes (frames and the two autofocus gaps; the HFD episode above 1.5 x baseline 22:18-23:34; frames with fewer than 5 comparisons, under the 21:06 cloud). Each header gives n, the robust sigma and a status word: C4 is 'Unstable' (σ 0.026, a slightly variable comparison), the others 'Stable'. Comparison quality table in the rail.
Plot wall in Charcoal.
Plot wall in Night Red: squares for comparisons, triangle for the check, circle for the target, all in the single red hue. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.

Plot wall interactions: the C4 cell expanded to the whole wall (cell menu or its expand tool, Esc restores), a selected time (frame 213, 21:52:33 UTC) shown as a dashed line on the cell and on the health strip, the synced crosshair at 21:30 on both, and the Selected point card reading every star at that time (V 9.311 ± 0.004, check +0.009, each comparison's residual), comparisons used, airmass, HFD / FWHM, sky, flags and the frame file name with 'Open frame'.
Plot wall at 1280 x 800 in Night Red: three columns still fit with the rail; long subtitles ellipsize. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.

Autofocus V-curve after a full run (good seeing): 7 coarse samples (hollow: not in the fit), 9 fine samples with HFD error bars, the weighted hyperbola fit with its ± 1 sigma envelope over the fitted window only, the asymptotes (the 'V', dotted), the chosen position in brass with its ± 1 sigma band ('best 1 281 ± 4'), the focuser line and the start position. Verdict in words: 'Measured. Focuser moved to 1 281; verification frame 2.56 px'. Readouts: HFD at best 2.63 ± 0.11 px, R² 0.996, χ²red 0.39.

The V-curve building point by point (step 11 of 17, fine sweep): the fit is redrawn after each fine sample from 4 samples on, and its vertex is shown as provisional (dashed neutral line, 'vertex 1 248 ± 22 · provisional') until the verdict: brass is only used for the decision.
V-curve after a full run, Charcoal.
V-curve after a full run, Night Red. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.

Poor seeing scenario, Night Red: larger error bars, a wider fit envelope and a wider position band ('best 1 235 ± 16'); still accepted because σc stays within a quarter of the 70-step fine step. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.

Flat-curve scenario, Charcoal: the verdict is 'Rejected: Flat HFD curve (2.9–3.3 px, span 11 % < 15 %). Focus unchanged, returned to 1 305.' No brass line is drawn and the best-focus readouts show '—'.

Conditions at 22:41:07 UTC: the rail card (every metric as a number with its last-hour sparkline and range) beside up to three small multiples on one UTC axis (Focus = HFD and dashed FWHM, Stars, Sky). The x range runs to the now-line, so the gap after the newest point is the age of the last frame ('Last frame 31 s ago · every 52 s'). The proposed attention rule is drawn where it fired: baseline 2.40 px (median of the first 20 frames), threshold 1.50 x = 3.60 px on a draggable, keyboard-operable handle, the episode from 22:18:13 shaded with a rug on every frame above the line, 'Attention' in the card and the header in words.
Conditions in Charcoal.
Conditions in Night Red: the attention state is carried by the outline, the left bar and the words, not by hue. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.

A frozen run: 'No frames' stops new frames while the clock runs. After max(2 x cadence, cadence + 60 s) the gap between the last frame and now is hatched on every facet, the now label reads 'no frame for …' and the header chip turns to 'No frame for … · expected every 52 s'. Between two healthy frames the same chart shows a short plain gap.
Conditions at 1280 x 800 in Charcoal: the rail card narrows to 300 px and the header chips shrink with an ellipsis instead of overflowing.

Visibility of SW And from Paris, night of 2026-11-01: twilight as luminance steps of --fg-muted (day, civil, nautical, astronomical, night; sunset 16:30, dusk 18:17, dawn 04:51, sunrise 06:38 UTC), altitude solid above the 30° minimum and dashed below it, the minimum altitude as a reference with a handle (a site setting), the transit labelled at the vertex (21:29, 70.5°), the Moon (49 % lit, rises 22:33) as a dashed neutral line with a direct label, the planned run as an outlined band with the frames taken so far as coverage (gap = the 20:31 autofocus), the now-line. UTC under the plot, local time (UTC+1) above, on the same x scale. Planning check in words: 'Planned run 18:40 → 02:05 stays above 30°'.
Visibility in Charcoal.
Visibility in Night Red: the twilight steps remain readable because they are luminance only. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.
Visibility of RR Lyr the same night: it transits at 16:32 in daylight and goes below 30° at 22:36, so the planning check turns into an attention chip, 'Planned run: last 3h 28m below 30°'.

Histogram of the live frame #269 (synthetic, consistent with the night: sky median 1 184 ADU, 16-ADU quantization of a 12-bit sensor, a star tail, 62 px saturated at 65 535). Auto stretch on: B 1 118, M 0.555 (at 1 243 ADU), W 1 344. What the stretch discards is stated: 0.24 % of pixels → black (hatched), 0.20 % → white; '62 px at 65 535 · beyond the range'. The dashed line is the display transfer, and the ramp under the axis is the exact mapping drawn in the viewer tint. B / W handles in brass, M on a second row so it never hides them.
Histogram in Charcoal.
Histogram in Night Red: the display ramp is red-only because it uses --viewer-tint (#d80000). Audit: 0 non-red pixels.

Keyboard operation: the W handle focused (focus ring) and moved two 16-ADU steps with the left arrow, from 1 344 to 1 312 ADU. Auto stretch turned itself off, the white-clipped region grew to 0.29 % and is labelled.

Full range (0-65 535 ADU) with log counts: the sky peak at the left, the star tail, and the sensor saturation rug at 65 535 in --danger. When B and W come close, their tabs lean away from each other so both values stay readable.

Mini-charts: a 32 px status bar where every chip carries its value in text and a chart adds trend or time (run progress as frame coverage with autofocus notches, last-frame age against the 52 s cadence with ticks at 1 x and the stale limit, HFD sparkline with its threshold and the word 'Attention', magnitude sparkline brighter-up, altitude over the night with the limit and now); a Run card and a Photometry card at rail width; the chip state matrix (normal, attention, stale, no data); and glance tiles at the 2 m scale (88 px primary digits, 66 px secondary, functional-spaces 2.5).
Mini-charts in Charcoal.
Mini-charts in Night Red: the stale hatching and attention outlines stay distinguishable by pattern and words. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.
Mini-charts at 1280 x 800: glance digits scale down with the tile (container query units) instead of overflowing; chips in the state matrix clip at their cell.

In context, 1440 x 900 with the lab chrome hidden: Observe › Run during the long watch (functional-spaces W4). Nav rail, toolbar with the proposed task modes (Run selected), the 16:9 image (a synthetic star field stand-in, defocused because HFD is 6.78 px at 22:41, with role overlays in the same shapes as the plots), the live light curve in the 299 px band under the image, the Run, Photometry, Conditions and Visibility cards in the 420 px rail, and the status bar with run, frame-age and attention chips. Only the charts are live; everything else is a static mock.
In context, Charcoal.
In context, Night Red: the whole screen, image included, is red-only. Audit: 0 non-red pixels.
In context at 1280 x 800: image 768 x 432, the band 290 px; the light curve stays two readable facets.
WebKit (WKWebView, macOS 26.5, 2x): the light curve renders like Chromium; mono tick labels, markers, error bars and the band are identical.

WebKit stress run: 5 000 → 5 520 points per facet appended one per frame at 2x: update median 6 ms, p95 7-8 ms, max 8-10 ms, 51-55 fps over two runs (WebKit rounds performance.now() to 1 ms; the probe window is on screen but transparent).
